source.text: Αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ ἐντολὴ ἡ ἐμὴ ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους καθὼς ἠγάπησα ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: This is the commandment the my, that you love one another just as I loved you.

en.L: This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandment, that you love one another just as I loved you.
en.B: My commandment is this: love one another in the same way that I have loved you.
en.R: My command to you is this: love each other the way I have loved you.

es.L: Este es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mandamiento: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros, como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} amé.
es.B: Mi mandamiento es este: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado.
es.R: Lo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} mando es esto: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros como yo {{plural_you:los|os}} he amado.

fr.L: Ceci est le commandement qui est le {{deity_pronoun:mien|Mien}} : que vous vous aimiez les uns les autres comme je vous ai aimés.
fr.B: Mon commandement, le voici : aimez-vous les uns les autres de la même manière que je vous ai aimés.
fr.R: Voici {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} commandement pour vous : vous devez vous aimer les uns les autres de la façon dont je vous ai aimés.

sw.L: Hii ndiyo amri {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kwamba mpendane kama vile nilivyowapenda.
sw.B: Amri {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni hii: pendaneni kwa namna ile ile niliyowapenda.
sw.R: Amri {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwenu ni hii: mpendane jinsi nilivyowapenda.

vi.L: Đây là điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là các con hãy yêu thương nhau như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu thương các con.
vi.B: Điều răn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thế này: hãy yêu thương nhau như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu thương các con.
vi.R: Điều răn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền cho các con là: hãy yêu thương nhau như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu thương các con.

ko.L: 이것이 나의 계명이다. 내가 너희를 사랑한 것처럼 너희가 서로 사랑하라는 것이다.
ko.B: 내 계명은 이것이다. 내가 너희를 사랑한 것과 같이 너희도 서로 사랑하여라.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 주는 계명은 이것이다. 내가 너희를 사랑한 것처럼 너희도 서로 사랑해라.

pt.L: Este é o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mandamento: que vocês se amem uns aos outros, assim como eu os amei.
pt.B: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mandamento é este: amem-se uns aos outros assim como eu amei vocês.
pt.R: O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} mandamento para vocês é este: amem uns aos outros do jeito que eu amei vocês.

decisions.choice: my commandment: the one command that is his own, the heart of all he commands
decisions.reason: The Greek says "the commandment, the one that is mine", which gives weight to "my". Verse 10 speaks of keeping his commandments in the plural; here they are gathered into one. It is the new commandment of 13:34, now given again after the picture of the vine (15:1-11).

decisions.choice: that you love one another: the content of the commandment
alternatives: purpose: given so that you will love one another
decisions.reason: After "this is my commandment" the word "that" introduces what the commandment says, as in 13:34. Verse 17 uses the same construction, where it may carry a note of purpose (see the decision there).

decisions.choice: just as I loved you: both the pattern and the ground of their love
decisions.reason: "Just as" gives the measure of their love and its source, as in 13:34 and 15:9. The past tense looks at his love as a whole, and the next verse shows how far it goes: to laying down his life (13:1; 15:13).

decisions.choice: love one another (L, B); love each other (R); commandment (L, B), command (R)
decisions.reason: The same English as the new commandment in 13:34 at each level, so that readers hear it given again. Balanced and Readable state the command directly after a colon, as 13:34 does; Readable says "command", the plainer word.

decisions.choice: mandamiento (L, B); amarse unos a otros
decisions.reason: As at 13:34, with the reflexive inside the ustedes / vosotros span.

decisions.choice: speech tenses: passé composé for the Greek past tenses ("je vous ai aimés", "je vous ai choisis"), at every level
alternatives: passé simple for the past tenses of speech
decisions.reason: This passage (15:12-17) is all Jesus's speech, so it has no narrative tense to settle; inside speech every level uses the passé composé, as people speak and as the rest of John's French does (see 1:19). French uses it both for a past act and for one whose effect lasts, so it serves for the Greek past of "I loved you" (meaning decision m3) without forcing a choice.

decisions.choice: le commandement qui est le {{deity_pronoun:mien|Mien}}
decisions.reason: The Greek gives weight to "my" by putting it after the noun with its own article (meaning decision m1). Literal shows that as in 15:9 ("l’amour qui est le mien"); Balanced and Readable say "mon commandement". The wording of the command follows 13:34 at each level, so readers hear it given again. Balanced begins with a plain "Mon", as a sentence-initial pronoun is written.

decisions.choice: Ta ... các con (Jesus to the disciples); điều răn; yêu thương
decisions.reason: As set for the whole book: Jesus says "Ta" of himself (the deity_pronoun span in mid-sentence) and "các con" to his disciples. "Điều răn" and "yêu thương" as in 13:34. Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체) and gives the Father the honorific ("께서", -시-)
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Recorded once for 15:12-17.

source.text: μείζονα ταύτης ἀγάπην οὐδεὶς ἔχει, ἵνα τις τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ θῇ ὑπὲρ τῶν φίλων αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Greater than this love no one has, that someone the life of him should lay down for the friends of him.

en.L: Greater love than this no one has, that someone lay down {{gender:their|his}} life for {{gender:their|his}} friends.
en.B: No one has a love greater than this: that someone lays down {{gender:their|his}} life for {{gender:their|his}} friends.
en.R: The greatest love anyone can show is to give up {{gender:their|his}} life for {{gender:their|his}} friends.

es.L: Nadie tiene amor mayor que este: que uno ponga su vida por sus amigos.
es.B: Nadie tiene un amor más grande que este: que alguien dé su vida por sus amigos.
es.R: El amor más grande que alguien puede mostrar es entregar su vida por sus amigos.

fr.L: Plus grand amour que celui-ci, personne ne l’a : que quelqu’un donne sa vie pour ses amis.
fr.B: Personne n’a d’amour plus grand que celui-ci : que quelqu’un donne sa vie pour ses amis.
fr.R: Le plus grand amour qu’on puisse montrer, c’est de donner sa vie pour ses amis.

sw.L: Upendo mkubwa kuliko huu hakuna aliye nao, kwamba mtu ayatoe maisha yake kwa ajili ya rafiki zake.
sw.B: Hakuna aliye na upendo unaozidi huu: mtu kuyatoa maisha yake kwa ajili ya rafiki zake.
sw.R: Upendo mkuu kabisa ambao mtu anaweza kuonyesha ni kuyatoa maisha yake kwa ajili ya rafiki zake.

vi.L: Không ai có tình yêu thương lớn hơn tình yêu thương này, là một người bỏ mạng sống mình vì bạn hữu mình.
vi.B: Không ai có tình yêu thương nào lớn hơn điều này: một người bỏ mạng sống mình vì bạn hữu mình.
vi.R: Tình yêu thương lớn nhất mà một người có thể bày tỏ là chết vì bạn bè mình.

ko.L: 이보다 더 큰 사랑을 가진 사람은 아무도 없다. 곧 누군가가 자기 친구들을 위하여 자기 목숨을 내려놓는 것이다.
ko.B: 친구들을 위하여 자기 목숨을 내놓는 것, 이보다 더 큰 사랑은 아무에게도 없다.
ko.R: 자기 친구들을 위해 목숨을 바치는 것보다 더 큰 사랑은 없다.

pt.L: Amor maior do que este ninguém tem: que alguém entregue a sua vida pelos seus amigos.
pt.B: Não existe amor maior do que este: alguém entregar a própria vida pelos seus amigos.
pt.R: O maior amor que alguém pode mostrar é dar a própria vida pelos seus amigos.

decisions.choice: that someone lay down his life: explains what "this" love is
alternatives: purpose: no one has greater love, in order to lay down his life
decisions.reason: "This" points forward, and the clause with "that" says what it is, as in verse 12. The verse is a general saying about any person, but it is spoken on the night before Jesus dies and describes what he is about to do.

decisions.choice: lay down his life: give up one's life freely, by dying
decisions.reason: It is the same expression as the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep (10:11, 15, 17-18) and as Peter's promise (13:37-38). Here "life" means life itself, not the soul as one part of a person. 1 John 3:16 draws the same line from Jesus's death to his followers' love.

decisions.choice: for his friends: on behalf of those he loves
alternatives: in place of his friends only
decisions.reason: The preposition means for the good of someone, as in 10:11 and 11:50-52. "Friends" is a word from the same family as one of the verbs for love; a friend is one who is loved. The next verses say who these friends are: the disciples (15:14-15). The saying measures love among friends; it does not deny that God's love reaches those who are not yet his friends (3:16; compare Romans 5:8-10).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}} life ... {{gender:their|his}} friends
decisions.reason: "Someone" and "anyone" mean any person, man or woman, so the pronouns take the gender setting (as in 12:25). Although the saying points to Jesus, it speaks of a general "someone", so the pronouns do not take the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: No one has a love greater than this: that someone lays down (B); The greatest love anyone can show is to give up (R)
alternatives: Greater love has no one than this
decisions.reason: The familiar wording of this verse comes from older translations. Balanced follows the Greek closely in normal English order; Readable states it positively, which is plainer. "Lay down" (Literal, Balanced) and "give up" (Readable) are the words used for this expression in 10:11-18 and 13:37-38.

decisions.choice: ponga (L); dé (B); entregar (R) su vida
decisions.reason: The same verbs as at 10:11 and 13:37 (meaning decision m2). Spanish "su" has no gender, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: sa vie ... ses amis, with no gender setting; donner sa vie
decisions.reason: The English needs the gender setting for "their" or "his". French "sa" and "ses" agree with the thing possessed, not with the owner, so they are already the same for a man or a woman and need no setting, as in Spanish. "Donner sa vie" is the same French as in 13:37-38 and the good shepherd (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: kuyatoa maisha yake
decisions.reason: The words of 10:11 and 13:37-38, so the reader hears the good shepherd and Peter's promise behind this saying. "Maisha" for this word, as in 12:25.

decisions.choice: "mình" (one's own), with no gender span
alternatives: của anh ấy / của chị ấy
decisions.reason: Where the English offers "their" or "his", the Vietnamese reflexive "mình" refers to any person, man or woman, so no gender setting is needed. "Bỏ mạng sống" (L, B) and "chết vì" (R) as in 13:37.

decisions.choice: no gender spans: "자기 목숨", "자기 친구들"
alternatives: gender setting spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean "자기" (one's own) is the same for men and women (style guide, section 7), so the gender setting has nothing to change. The verbs follow 13:37: "내려놓다" (L), "내놓다" (B), "바치다" (R).

decisions.choice: a sua vida / a própria vida, os seus amigos, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English needs a gender setting for "their/his". The Portuguese possessive agrees with the thing possessed, not with the owner, so "a sua vida" and "os seus amigos" already say nothing about whether "alguém" is a man or a woman.

source.text: ὑμεῖς φίλοι μού ἐστε ἐὰν ποιῆτε ἃ ἐγὼ ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: You friends of me are if you do what I command you.

en.L: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friends if you do what I command you.
en.B: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friends if you carry out what I command you.
en.R: You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} friends if you do what I tell you to do.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} amigos, si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} mando.
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} amigos si {{plural_you:cumplen|cumplís}} lo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} mando.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} amigos si {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} lo que yo {{plural_you:les|os}} digo.

fr.L: Vous, vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} amis si vous faites ce que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je vous commande.
fr.B: Vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} amis si vous accomplissez ce que je vous commande.
fr.R: Vous êtes {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} amis si vous faites ce que je vous dis de faire.

sw.L: Ninyi ni rafiki {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} ikiwa mnafanya yale {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ninayowaagiza.
sw.R: Ninyi ni rafiki {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} mkifanya yale ninayowaambia mfanye.

vi.L: Các con là bạn hữu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nếu các con làm những gì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền cho các con.
vi.B: Các con là bạn hữu của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nếu các con thực hiện những điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền dạy các con.
vi.R: Các con là bạn của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nếu các con làm theo những gì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo các con.

ko.L: 너희는, 내가 너희에게 명령하는 것을 행하면, 나의 친구들이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 명령하는 것을 너희가 행하면, 너희는 나의 친구이다.
ko.R: 내가 하라고 하는 것을 너희가 하면 너희는 내 친구다.

pt.L: Vocês são {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} amigos se fizerem o que eu lhes ordeno.
pt.B: Vocês são {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} amigos se cumprirem o que eu lhes ordeno.
pt.R: Vocês são {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} amigos se fizerem o que eu mando vocês fazerem.

decisions.choice: friends: those loved and trusted, who share in another's purposes
decisions.reason: The word follows straight on from "his friends" in verse 13: the disciples are the friends for whom Jesus lays down his life. In Israel's Scriptures Abraham is called God's friend (2 Chronicles 20:7; Isaiah 41:8), and God speaks with Moses as one speaks with a friend (Exodus 33:11). John the Baptist calls himself the friend of the bridegroom (3:29), and Jesus calls Lazarus "our friend" (11:11).

decisions.choice: if you do what I command you: the mark of friendship, not the price of it
alternatives: a condition they must meet to earn his friendship
decisions.reason: The friendship rests on his choice and his love (verses 13 and 16); doing what he commands shows that they are what he says they are, as love is shown by keeping his commands in 14:15, 21 and 15:10. The pronouns "you" and "I" are both stressed in the Greek.

decisions.choice: carry out what I command you (B); do what I tell you to do (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses an ordinary verb for obeying instructions; Readable uses plain words. "Command" in Literal and Balanced keeps the link with verses 12 and 17.

decisions.choice: cumplen (B); hacen lo que les digo (R)
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: bạn hữu (L, B); bạn (R)
decisions.reason: "Bạn hữu" is the fuller written word for a close, trusted friend; Readable uses the everyday "bạn".

source.text: οὐκέτι λέγω ὑμᾶς δούλους, ὅτι ὁ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν τί ποιεῖ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος· ὑμᾶς δὲ εἴρηκα φίλους, ὅτι πάντα ἃ ἤκουσα παρὰ τοῦ πατρός μου ἐγνώρισα ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: No longer I call you slaves, because the slave not knows what is doing of him the master; you but I have called friends, because all things that I heard from the Father of me I made known to you.

en.L: No longer do I call you slaves, because the slave does not know what his master is doing; but I have called you friends, because all that I heard from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father I made known to you.
en.B: I do not call you servants any longer, since a servant is not aware of what his master is doing. I have called you friends instead, because I have made known to you everything I heard from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.
en.R: I do not call you servants anymore. A servant does not know what his master is doing. But I call you friends, because I have told you everything I heard from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Father.

es.L: Ya no {{plural_you:los|os}} llamo esclavos, porque el esclavo no sabe lo que hace su señor; pero {{plural_you:los|os}} he llamado amigos, porque todo lo que oí de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} he dado a conocer.
es.B: Ya no {{plural_you:los|os}} llamo siervos, porque un siervo no sabe lo que hace su señor. Más bien, {{plural_you:los|os}} he llamado amigos, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} he dado a conocer todo lo que oí de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre.
es.R: Ya no {{plural_you:los|os}} llamo siervos. Un siervo no sabe lo que hace su señor. Pero yo {{plural_you:los|os}} llamo amigos, porque {{plural_you:les|os}} he contado todo lo que oí de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} Padre.

fr.L: Je ne vous appelle plus esclaves, parce que l’esclave ne sait pas ce que fait son maître ; mais je vous ai appelés amis, parce que tout ce que j’ai entendu de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père, je vous l’ai fait connaître.
fr.B: Je ne vous appelle plus des serviteurs, car un serviteur n’est pas au courant de ce que fait son maître. Je vous ai plutôt appelés des amis, parce que je vous ai révélé tout ce que j’ai entendu auprès de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.
fr.R: Je ne vous appelle plus serviteurs. Un serviteur ne sait pas ce que fait son maître. Mais je vous appelle amis, parce que je vous ai raconté tout ce que j’ai entendu de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} Père.

sw.L: Siwaiti tena watumwa, kwa kuwa mtumwa hajui kile ambacho bwana wake anafanya; lakini ninyi nimewaita rafiki, kwa kuwa kila kitu nilichosikia kwa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} nimewafahamisha.
sw.B: Siwaiti tena watumishi, kwa kuwa mtumishi hajui bwana wake anachofanya. Badala yake nimewaita rafiki, kwa sababu nimewajulisha kila kitu nilichosikia kutoka kwa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.R: Siwaiti watumishi tena. Mtumishi hajui bwana wake anachofanya. Lakini ninawaita rafiki, kwa sababu nimewaambia kila kitu nilichosikia kutoka kwa Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Ta không còn gọi các con là nô lệ nữa, vì nô lệ không biết chủ mình làm gì; nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gọi các con là bạn hữu, vì mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe từ Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã cho các con biết.
vi.B: Ta không còn gọi các con là đầy tớ nữa, vì đầy tớ không biết việc chủ mình đang làm. Thay vào đó, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gọi các con là bạn hữu, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã cho các con biết mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe từ Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta không gọi các con là đầy tớ nữa. Đầy tớ không biết chủ mình đang làm gì. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} gọi các con là bạn, vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói cho các con mọi điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nghe từ Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 이제 더 이상 너희를 종들이라 부르지 않는다. 종은 자기 주인이 무엇을 하는지 알지 못하기 때문이다. 그러나 나는 너희를 친구들이라 불렀다. 내가 내 아버지께 들은 모든 것을 너희에게 알려 주었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이제 나는 너희를 더 이상 종이라고 부르지 않는다. 종은 주인이 하는 일을 알지 못하기 때문이다. 오히려 나는 너희를 친구라고 불렀다. 내가 내 아버지께 들은 것을 모두 너희에게 알려 주었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 나는 이제 너희를 종이라고 부르지 않는다. 종은 주인이 무엇을 하는지 모른다. 그러나 나는 너희를 친구라고 부른다. 내가 내 아버지께 들은 것을 너희에게 다 말해 주었기 때문이다.

pt.L: Já não chamo vocês de escravos, porque o escravo não sabe o que o senhor dele faz; mas eu os tenho chamado de amigos, porque tudo o que ouvi do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai eu lhes dei a conhecer.
pt.B: Já não chamo vocês de servos, pois o servo não sabe o que o senhor dele está fazendo. Em vez disso, eu os chamei de amigos, porque lhes dei a conhecer tudo o que ouvi do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai.
pt.R: Eu não chamo mais vocês de servos. Um servo não sabe o que o senhor dele está fazendo. Mas eu chamo vocês de amigos, porque contei a vocês tudo o que ouvi do {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} Pai.

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master, who carries out orders without being told their purpose
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary one for a slave, someone who was another's property (8:34-35; 13:16). Here the point is the slave's place in the household: he is told what to do, not why. Jesus has called himself their Lord (13:13-14) and will remind them that "a slave is not greater than his master" (15:20).

decisions.choice: his master: the owner in the picture of the household
decisions.reason: In this sentence the word means simply the slave's owner. It is the same word as "Lord" in 13:13-16, so the hearers can see that Jesus is speaking about how he treats them; he does not stop being their Lord.

decisions.choice: no longer slaves but friends: the change is in what they are told, not in whether they serve
alternatives: they are freed from serving and obeying him
decisions.reason: The reason Jesus gives is about knowledge: a slave is not told his master's purposes, but Jesus has told them what he heard from the Father. They still do what he commands (verse 14), and in 15:20 he still calls them slaves who are not greater than their master. Compare Genesis 18:17, where God does not hide from Abraham, his friend, what he is about to do.

decisions.choice: all that I heard from my Father I made known to you: everything the Father gave him to tell them
alternatives: every truth there is to know
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks only what he hears from the Father (8:26, 40; 12:49-50). "All" means all that the Father has given him for them; in 16:12 he still has more to tell them, which the Spirit will teach (16:13). The past tense looks back over his teaching as a whole, while "I have called you friends" is a perfect: they are now his friends.

decisions.choice: slaves, slave (L); servants, servant (B, R); master (every level)
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, "slave" in Literal, as the style guide has it and as at 13:16 and 15:20. The style guide keeps "slave" where slave is set against free, but here the contrast is with "friends", and it turns on what they are told, not on freedom: they still serve and obey (meaning decision m3). "Servant" keeps that contrast; meaning decision m1 keeps that a slave was owned. "Master" is the word of 13:16 and 15:20, used because here it means a slave's owner (meaning decision m2). "His" refers to the figure in the saying and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: I have made known to you everything I heard (B); I have told you everything I heard (R)
alternatives: all that I heard from my Father I made known to you (Literal)
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "all that I heard" first; Balanced and Readable use normal English order and the English perfect, since the telling is complete at the time he speaks. Balanced says a servant "is not aware" of what his master is doing, which is the sense of "does not know" here.

decisions.choice: esclavos, esclavo (L); siervos, siervo (B, R); señor
decisions.reason: The same words as at 13:16 (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R); son maître (every level)
decisions.reason: As the French brief and the English: "esclave" at Literal, "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable, since the point is the servant's place in the household, not slavery itself (meaning decision m1). The owner is "son maître": in French "seigneur" would sound feudal. The Greek word is the one translated "Seigneur" in 13:13-16, a link French cannot keep (m2).

decisions.choice: watumwa, mtumwa (L); watumishi, mtumishi (B, R); bwana wake, lowercase
decisions.reason: "Mtumishi" (servant) in Balanced and Readable and "mtumwa" (slave) in Literal, as the English has it; the contrast with "rafiki" (friend) is about what they are told, not about freedom (meaning decision m3). The master is the owner in the picture, so "bwana" is lowercase and "wake" carries no reader setting, as at 13:16 and in verse 20.

decisions.choice: nô lệ (L); đầy tớ (B, R); chủ
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for doulos, as in the English: "nô lệ" (slave) at Literal, "đầy tớ" (servant) at Balanced and Readable; also in 15:20.

decisions.choice: "종" and "주인" at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide (section 6) sets "종" for doulos at every level, where the English Balanced and Readable say "servant"; Korean "종" covers both one who is owned and one who serves. "노예" would put slavery itself in the foreground, which is not the point here.

decisions.choice: o senhor dele, at every level
decisions.reason: "Senhor" is the word for a slave's master and is the same word the disciples use for Jesus ("Senhor", 13:13-16), as in the Greek (meaning decision m2); "dono" or "patrão" would lose the link. "Dele" rather than "seu", which a reader addressed as "vocês" could take as "your".

source.text: οὐχ ὑμεῖς με ἐξελέξασθε, ἀλλ’ ἐγὼ ἐξελεξάμην ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἔθηκα ὑμᾶς ἵνα ὑμεῖς ὑπάγητε καὶ καρπὸν φέρητε καὶ ὁ καρπὸς ὑμῶν μένῃ, ἵνα ὅ τι ἂν αἰτήσητε τὸν πατέρα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί μου δῷ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Not you me chose, but I chose you, and appointed you that you should go and fruit bear and the fruit of you should remain, that whatever you ask the Father in the name of me he may give you.

en.L: You did not choose {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, but I chose you, and I appointed you that you should go and bear fruit and your fruit should remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give you.
en.B: You did not choose {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; I chose you. I appointed you for this: to go and bear fruit, and for your fruit to remain, so that the Father may give you whatever you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.
en.R: You did not choose {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I chose you. I gave you the task of going out and bearing fruit that will remain. And so the Father will give you whatever you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name.

es.L: No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:eligieron|elegisteis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, sino que yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:los|os}} he puesto para que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} y {{plural_you:den|deis}} fruto, y {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} fruto permanezca, para que todo lo que {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} al Padre en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:se lo|os lo}} dé.
es.B: No {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:eligieron|elegisteis}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Y {{plural_you:los|os}} he puesto para esto: para que {{plural_you:vayan|vayáis}} y {{plural_you:den|deis}} fruto, y para que {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} fruto permanezca. Así el Padre {{plural_you:les|os}} dará todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes no|Vosotros no}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:eligieron|elegisteis}} a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Yo {{plural_you:los|os}} elegí a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} he dado la tarea de salir y dar un fruto que permanezca. Y así el Padre {{plural_you:les|os}} dará todo lo que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre.

fr.L: Vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas choisi, vous ; mais c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui vous ai choisis, et je vous ai placés pour que vous, vous partiez et portiez du fruit, et que votre fruit demeure, afin que, quoi que vous demandiez au Père en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous le donne.
fr.B: Vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas choisi ; c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui vous ai choisis. Je vous ai établis pour que vous partiez porter du fruit, et que ce fruit demeure, afin que le Père vous donne tout ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.
fr.R: Vous ne {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}avez pas choisi. C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui vous ai choisis. Je vous ai donné la mission de partir et de porter du fruit, un fruit qui demeure. Et ainsi, le Père vous donnera tout ce que vous {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demanderez en {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom.

sw.L: Ninyi hamkunichagua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, bali {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliwachagua ninyi, nikawateua ili ninyi mwende mkazae matunda, na matunda yenu yakae, ili chochote mtakachomwomba Baba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} awapatie.
sw.B: Hamkunichagua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliwachagua ninyi. Niliwateua kwa ajili ya hili: mwende mkazae matunda, na matunda yenu yakae, ili Baba awape chochote mtakachomwomba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.
sw.R: Hamkunichagua {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Mimi niliwachagua ninyi. Niliwapa kazi ya kwenda na kuzaa matunda yatakayokaa. Na hivyo Baba atawapa chochote mtakachomwomba kwa jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}.

vi.L: Không phải các con đã chọn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn các con, và đã lập các con để các con đi và sinh trái, và trái của các con được còn lại, để bất cứ điều gì các con cầu xin Cha trong danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ ban cho các con.
vi.B: Các con đã không chọn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn các con. Ta đã lập các con để các con đi và sinh trái, và để trái của các con còn lại lâu dài, hầu cho Cha ban cho các con bất cứ điều gì các con nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà cầu xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Không phải các con chọn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chọn các con. Ta đã giao cho các con nhiệm vụ ra đi và ra trái, là thứ trái sẽ còn lại lâu dài. Như vậy, Cha sẽ ban cho các con bất cứ điều gì các con nhân danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mà xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 너희가 나를 택한 것이 아니라 내가 너희를 택하였고, 너희를 세웠다. 너희가 가서 열매를 맺고 너희 열매가 머물러 있게 하려는 것이며, 너희가 내 이름으로 아버지께 무엇을 구하든지 그분께서 너희에게 주시게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 너희가 나를 택한 것이 아니다. 내가 너희를 택하였다. 그리고 너희를 세웠다. 너희가 가서 열매를 맺고, 그 열매가 늘 남아 있게 하려는 것이다. 그래서 너희가 내 이름으로 아버지께 무엇을 구하든지 아버지께서 주시게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 너희가 나를 선택한 것이 아니다. 내가 너희를 선택했다. 나는 너희에게 나가서 열매를 맺는 일을 맡겼다. 그 열매는 오래 남을 것이다. 그래서 너희가 내 이름으로 아버지께 무엇을 구하든지 아버지께서 주실 것이다.

pt.L: Não foram vocês que {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escolheram, mas eu escolhi vocês, e os designei para que vocês vão e deem fruto, e o fruto de vocês permaneça, para que tudo o que pedirem ao Pai em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes dê.
pt.B: Vocês não {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escolheram; eu escolhi vocês. Eu os designei para isto: para irem e darem fruto, e para que o fruto de vocês permaneça, a fim de que o Pai lhes dê tudo o que vocês {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} pedirem em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome.
pt.R: Vocês não {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} escolheram. Eu escolhi vocês. Eu dei a vocês a tarefa de ir e dar fruto que permaneça. E assim o Pai vai dar a vocês tudo o que pedirem a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} em {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} nome.

decisions.choice: You did not choose me, but I chose you: the usual order is reversed
decisions.reason: In that time a student would usually choose a teacher and attach himself to him. Here the choice was Jesus's, as he says in 6:70 and 13:18. Both "you" and "I" are stressed in the Greek.

decisions.choice: appointed: set in a place for a task
decisions.reason: The verb means to put or set someone in a position for a purpose. It is the same verb as "lay down" in verse 13, though there it is used in a fixed expression for giving one's life. Nothing here describes a formal rite; the task follows in the next words.

decisions.choice: go and bear fruit, and your fruit remain: the vine picture of 15:1-8, now with their going out
alternatives: fruit means only their own good character
decisions.reason: "Fruit" and "remain" pick up the words of the vine (15:2, 4-5, 8). The fruit is the life that grows from remaining in him, shown in love (15:12) and in people brought to him (4:36; 12:24). "Go" adds that they are sent (17:18; 20:21). The fruit is to last, not wither like a cut branch (15:6).

decisions.choice: the second "that": a further purpose of his choosing and appointing them
alternatives: result of their fruit bearing: when they bear fruit, the Father answers their prayers
decisions.reason: The first "that" gives the purpose of the appointing: to go, bear fruit, and have their fruit remain. The second can be read as another purpose of the same appointing, or as what follows from bearing fruit. The two readings come to much the same thing: those who remain in him and bear fruit ask and receive (15:7).

decisions.choice: in my name: as those who belong to him, on his authority
alternatives: using his name as a formula
decisions.reason: To ask in someone's name is to ask as his representative and by his authority. Jesus promises that such requests will be answered (14:13-14; 16:23-24).

decisions.choice: appointed (L, B), gave you the task (R); remain (every level)
decisions.reason: "Remain" is this book's word for the verb in the vine passage (15:4-10), so the link stays visible; Readable keeps it in the phrase "fruit that will remain". Readable says what the appointing was for rather than using "appointed".

decisions.choice: the Father may give you whatever you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name (B); And so the Father will give you (R)
alternatives: whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make "the Father" the subject and supply "him" after "ask", which is normal English. Readable starts a new sentence with "And so", which keeps the link of purpose and result (meaning decision m4) in short sentences.

decisions.choice: he puesto (L, B); les he dado la tarea (R); permanezca (every level)
decisions.reason: Set in a place for a task (meaning decision m2). "Permanecer" for the lasting fruit, as with the vine.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} for the Father
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" and the clitic "le" (to him) for the Father both take the setting, by the book-wide rule (1:1).

decisions.choice: placés (L); établis (B); donné la mission (R); demeure (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb means to set someone in a place for a task (meaning decision m2): Literal "placer" keeps the picture, Balanced "établir" is the usual word for appointing, and Readable says what they were set there to do. "Demeure" keeps the key verb of the vine passage (15:4-10), as the English keeps "remain". French marks the stressed "I" (m1) with "c’est moi qui", a pronoun for Christ with the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: còn lại (for the fruit)
decisions.reason: Meno is "ở lại" or "ở trong" where people remain in Jesus; for fruit Vietnamese needs "còn lại" (last, stay). Balanced and Readable add "lâu dài" (lasting) to make the sense plain.

decisions.choice: "늘 남아 있게" (B); "오래 남을 것이다" (R); "머물러 있게" (L)
decisions.reason: Said of fruit, menō means to last; Korean "머무르다" is natural for persons, not for fruit, so Balanced and Readable say "남아 있다". Literal keeps "머무르다" so the link with 15:4-10 stays visible.

source.text: ταῦτα ἐντέλλομαι ὑμῖν ἵνα ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους.

records.literal_gloss: These things I command you, that you love one another.

en.L: These things I command you, that you love one another.
en.B: I give you these commands so that you will love one another.
en.R: I give you these commands so that you will love each other.

es.L: Esto {{plural_you:les|os}} mando: que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros.
es.B: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} doy estos mandamientos para que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} doy estos mandatos para que {{plural_you:se amen|os améis}} unos a otros.

fr.L: Ces choses, je vous les commande : que vous vous aimiez les uns les autres.
fr.B: Je vous donne ces commandements pour que vous vous aimiez les uns les autres.
fr.R: Je vous donne ces commandements pour que vous vous aimiez les uns les autres.

vi.L: Những điều này {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền cho các con, là để các con yêu thương nhau.
vi.B: Ta truyền cho các con những điều này để các con yêu thương nhau.
vi.R: Ta truyền dặn các con những điều ấy để các con yêu thương nhau.

ko.L: 이것들을 내가 너희에게 명령한다. 너희가 서로 사랑하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 너희에게 이것들을 명령하는 것은, 너희가 서로 사랑하게 하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 너희에게 이렇게 명령하는 것은 너희가 서로 사랑하게 하려는 것이다.

pt.L: Estas coisas eu lhes ordeno: que vocês se amem uns aos outros.
pt.B: Eu lhes dou estes mandamentos para que vocês se amem uns aos outros.
pt.R: Eu dou estes mandamentos a vocês para que vocês amem uns aos outros.

decisions.choice: these things: what he has just said in verses 12-16
decisions.reason: "These things" is plural and most naturally points back to what he has been saying. The verse closes the section that verse 12 opened with the same command, "love one another".

decisions.choice: that you love one another: the aim of all he commands
alternatives: content: this is what I command, love one another
decisions.reason: With a plural "these things" before it, the clause with "that" reads most easily as purpose: all his commands lead to their love for each other. It can also give the content of the command, as in verse 12. Either way, love for one another is the point of what he commands.

decisions.choice: that you love one another (L); so that you will love one another (B), each other (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "that", which can carry either sense (meaning decision m2). Balanced and Readable state the purpose. "Love one another" and "love each other" are the same English as 13:34 and 15:12.

decisions.choice: para que se amen unos a otros
decisions.reason: As in English (meaning decision m2).
